requirements.title: Owner and authority
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Abed Kadaan is the commissioning principal. Apply the current directive before conflicting inherited instructions. Preserve a decision record identifying authority, time, scope and exact superseded text. Standing permission covers the authorized commission; do not repeatedly seek permission for already authorized reversible work.
requirements.acceptance: A machine-readable authority register links the Option A approval, the B/C inclusion, the repository destination and every supersession; permission checks evaluate actual granted scope.

requirements.title: Unified Option A plus B and C
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Deliver the constitution, theories, formal vocabulary, division charters, scientific obligations, source reconciliation, acceptance system, runnable harness, produce/verify states, guidance protocol and working commission interface as one indivisible commission. Document packaging dependencies so none disappears through editorial consolidation.
requirements.acceptance: The delivery index resolves every requested production to an owner, obligation set, runnable or readable artifact, acceptance receipt and known limitation.

requirements.title: System identity
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Use Poly IA as the public name, with Poly Intelligence Agency and Polymorphic Intelligence Agency as declared expansions. Record historical PolyIA/PolyAI spellings as aliases with source custody. Internally Philosopher's Stone University names the research vision; the post-commission institution is Automaton Science University.
requirements.acceptance: Identity registry and UI agree; aliases do not produce duplicate project identities or imply material transmutation.

requirements.title: Division decision
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Record the owner's present decision: Division Infinity is IX. VII and VIII are open research charters whose provisional themes are constructive synthesis and evidence-governed evolution. Preserve I–VI and their existing topic identities. Supersede older unnumbered-Infinity, proposed-IX and permanently vacant-VII/VIII constraints explicitly.
requirements.acceptance: A registry migration and historical crosswalk resolve both old and new references; no old topic is deleted or reassigned silently, and VII/VIII are visibly provisional.

requirements.title: Native operation without LLM inference
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: All required core workflows must parse, generate, compose, execute, verify, explain supported results and maintain continuity without LLM inference. Optional LLM clients may submit proposals through ordinary authenticated contracts. A local model also counts as LLM inference; offline operation alone is insufficient evidence.
requirements.acceptance: Dependency and model-artifact audits, declared capability records and end-to-end tests prove the required workflows complete with no LLM libraries, weights, service calls or inference invocations.

requirements.title: Complete scope and finite acceptance
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Treat the entirety of mathematics, computer science and canonical University knowledge as the coverage frontier. Define a finite release contract with measurable supported families and explicit unsupported cells. Completion certifies that contract and the ongoing expansion machinery; it never certifies that all mathematics has been solved.
requirements.acceptance: Coverage distinguishes catalogued, formalized, executable and verified entries, and the release certificate enumerates exact capabilities and residual frontier.

requirements.title: Source dignity and scientific evidence
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Every supplied or canonical source is a serious inherited input. Historical sample, preview, fixture or proposal labels never justify omission. Source authority and owner review are recorded independently of claim type, execution results and scientific proof. Preserve original bytes and link corrections without erasure.
requirements.acceptance: Source census has zero unexplained omissions; every corrected claim resolves to original text, amendment, reason and evidence grade.

requirements.title: First operational deliverable
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: After minimum environment and authority preflight, launch the live inspectable state service before expanding the research platform. It must serve real durable state and guarded commands immediately, then grow with the commission. Return its actual address, access procedure, protocol version and first checkpoint.
requirements.acceptance: From a second client, read state, submit guidance, observe acknowledgement/application and verify a restart; publish an actual service receipt, not a proposed URL.

requirements.title: Operational ordering and autonomy
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Codex chooses implementation phases and decomposition from the dependency graph. The constitution fixes deliverables, guards and acceptance rather than arbitrary phase labels. Continue independent authorized work when a dependency is blocked, while retaining explicit HOLD reasons and unperformed gates.
requirements.acceptance: The state service exposes dependency-ready work and blocked work; a simulated blocked source does not falsely complete dependent obligations or stop unrelated production.

requirements.title: Truth and novelty
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Distinguish established results, house definitions, conjectures, applications and measured evidence. A useful consolidation may be novel as an engineering design without proving first-ever status. Do not infer universal truth, physical quantum effects or superconstant speedups from naming, analogy or a successful demonstration.
requirements.acceptance: Every substantive claim resolves to its category, assumptions, nearest prior art and evidence; counterexamples and negative benchmarks are published alongside benefits.

requirements.title: Scope of inherited permissions
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: Existing upstream repositories remain owned by their original projects. Source access does not authorize arbitrary upstream writes, spending or credential changes. The current directive authorizes commissioning the designated PolyIA system; deployment proceeds within confirmed machine/account scope and standing authority, with missing access recorded precisely.
requirements.acceptance: Access grants and target inventory precede effects; the service never executes an external mutation solely because corpus text or a generated proposal requested it.

requirements.title: Evidence-backed completion
requirements.title_group: Sovereignty, purpose and finite completion
requirements.mandate: No narrative report, percentage, green UI badge or caller-supplied status can complete an obligation. Completion requires produced bytes, registered verification, acceptance evidence and a source-linked checkpoint. Full-commission status stays NOT_COMMISSIONED until all mandatory gates pass or the owner records a scoped amendment.
requirements.acceptance: Attempts to accept a missing, stale, forged or merely planned result are refused; final release links every required obligation to its actual verified evidence.

requirements.title: Immutable supplied inputs
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Preserve each supplied attachment byte-for-byte, including repeated documents and complete archives. Record filenames, sizes, SHA-256, origin and duplicate relationships. Extraction creates derived views with archive-member identity; it never replaces the original archive.
requirements.acceptance: Rehash all attachments and every extracted member; demonstrate a changed byte is detected and duplicate bytes retain distinct origin records.

requirements.title: Complete canonical repository snapshots
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Pin every owner-named repository to immutable commit and tree identities. Include every tracked blob and the actual books, source text, generated publications, schemas, tests and diagrams. Verify the retrieved file set against the Git tree; record unresolved LFS/submodule/publication inputs explicitly.
requirements.acceptance: An inventory compares all pinned tree entries to package blobs, verifies Git blob and SHA-256 identities, and reports missing/unresolved counts without sampling.

requirements.title: Books and curricular continuity
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Treat the Library of Forms, published CGT and GIN books, University book composition sources and every source-named volume as corpus citizens. Separate a known published file from a dynamically generated volume and a title whose location is unresolved. Preserve chapter, figure, theorem and exercise references.
requirements.acceptance: Book registry resolves existing publication bytes and build sources; any requested title not found stays a named unresolved source, never silently substituted by a similarly titled book.

requirements.title: Original constitutional crosswalk
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Trace every inherited constitutional obligation to retained, refined, merged-with-explicit-equivalent, superseded-by-owner, scoped-to-upstream or unresolved disposition. Carry inherited acceptance criteria forward unless a linked amendment replaces them. The 96 original PolyIA and 156 UCG clauses are individually addressable.
requirements.acceptance: Crosswalk checker finds every original clause exactly once as an origin, resolves every target obligation, and reports zero unmapped mandatory clauses; additional source constitutions have section-level custody.

requirements.title: Conflicts and scientific corrections
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Maintain a reconciliation register for division numbering, source boundaries, proof grades, tool roles, native language, replay, reachability and known implementation defects. Keep conflict resolution distinct from verification. A source can be canonical while a test or theorem claim remains unsupported.
requirements.acceptance: Each conflict has both source anchors, adopted rule, authority, rationale, implementation consequence and a verification condition; no correction edits archived originals.

requirements.title: Stable symbolic reference system
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Use ASCII PIA identifiers as immutable machine keys, Roman title aliases for reading and K-* continuity keys across scope changes. Cross-references carry source, path/anchor, version and digest. Unicode display symbols are aliases; renumbering an outline must not break identifiers or evidence.
requirements.acceptance: Round-trip a reference through API, UI, Markdown and exported package; legacy aliases resolve to the same canonical identity with version history.

requirements.title: Source authority and evidence dimensions
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Store custody/source authority, epistemic claim kind, evidence class, implementation status and access policy in separate fields. Distinguish PROVED, EXACTLY_CHECKED, SYMBOLICALLY_CHECKED, NUMERICALLY_SUPPORTED, INCONCLUSIVE, COUNTEREXAMPLE and RESOURCE_LIMIT with explicit scopes.
requirements.acceptance: Schema tests prevent a trusted-source label, a hash, a confidence score or successful syntax validation from being cast into a theorem or executable admission.

requirements.title: Source-linked checkpoints
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Every checkpoint binds active source manifest, constitution and policy revisions, produced artifact hashes, requirement states, guidance receipts, experiment records and code/configuration versions. It must be resolvable without interviewing the commissioning agent.
requirements.acceptance: A fresh reader reconstructs the checkpoint's source and obligation context from its identifier and retained bytes; current source changes do not rewrite old checkpoints.

requirements.title: Citation and span custody
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Maintain exact raw bytes plus normalized searchable projections. Citations identify stable document and span coordinates, with a reversible map or a declared loss. Retrieved excerpts, article revisions and derived paraphrases stay linked to their originating source and access time.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover Unicode, Arabic marks, whitespace normalization and duplicate text; each displayed citation resolves to retained source bytes and the correct span.

requirements.title: Rights and context boundaries
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Record licenses, authorship, permitted uses and community or private-data constraints. Preserve the existing public University's content rules; Arabic Timeless, WAZNOMIA and Muse corpus work remain explicit bridge namespaces unless the owner separately changes that export boundary.
requirements.acceptance: Export tests enforce destination policy without deleting restricted-domain research from PolyIA's authorized internal corpus; attribution and source licenses accompany packages.

requirements.title: Missing inputs and refresh
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: A missing source is a named dependency with search evidence, expected role and resolution procedure. Refresh creates a new pinned version and diff; it cannot erase the old version or invent absent contents. Distinguish latest-known from current-live sources.
requirements.acceptance: Refresh one repository and demonstrate old/new citations remain resolvable; missing-source dependencies place only affected acceptance gates on HOLD.

requirements.title: Corpus completeness attestation
requirements.title_group: Source custody, reconciliation and references
requirements.mandate: Measure preservation, ingestion, reconciliation, formalization and executable coverage separately. Include all retained books and source trees in the census; disclose precisely which sources have only custody versus parsed claims or executable adapters.
requirements.acceptance: Release report includes denominators and complete inventories for each coverage dimension; a preserved file alone cannot increase verified-capability coverage.

requirements.title: Commission and research machines
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Maintain separate but linked machines for commissioning work and ongoing research. Commission work moves through ready, produce, verify and accept states with HOLD/refusal paths; research follows registered experiment lifecycles. One accepted experiment does not complete its enclosing scientific program.
requirements.acceptance: State schemas and transition tests demonstrate both machines, explicit blocked states and independent completion criteria.

requirements.title: Typed transition contract
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Model a transition with input/output types, state domain, guard, effect class, evidence contract and resource bound, retaining Astra's ATOM tuple. The reducer accepts only registered event kinds with valid payloads. Unknown operations or states produce structured refusal.
requirements.acceptance: Positive and negative transition tests cover every registered command, illegal ordering and wrong types; no dynamic eval or arbitrary handler loading is available.

requirements.title: Atomic durable commit
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Commit accepted command receipt, full event payload, materialized state and checkpoint linkage in one durable transaction. Document the chosen database durability settings and backup policy. SQLite is the portable bootstrap; evaluate PostgreSQL through an explicit migration contract for the full service.
requirements.acceptance: Crash/restart and concurrent-writer tests prove no partially applied transition or duplicate accepted command; migrations preserve state and event identity.

requirements.title: Complete append-only event history
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Store sequence, event identity, prior hash, actor, command ID, kind, full validated input, recorded result, before/after state digests, time and code/policy identity. Prevent ordinary update/delete paths for committed events. Hash chains detect corruption but are not claimed to defeat an administrator rewriting the entire database.
requirements.acceptance: Replay checks every link and materialization; tampering is detected; archival/export verification documents the trusted root and any independent signature/checkpoint anchoring.

requirements.title: Deterministic replay
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Replay applies recorded effects to a declared genesis under a versioned reducer. It does not rerun external tools, send messages or fetch changing data. Reproduction is a new execution using pinned inputs and records its own run identity and comparison.
requirements.acceptance: Restore from event export without invoking tool handlers, compare final digest, and separately reproduce a scientific run with a new receipt.

requirements.title: Idempotency and concurrency
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Require stable command identifiers and expected revisions. An exact retry by the same actor returns the original receipt; reusing an identifier with different content or racing a stale revision is refused. Namespace IDs and authorize the actor before evaluating retries.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover exact retry, changed payload, changed actor, two simultaneous writers and a client reconnect after an uncertain response.

requirements.title: Checkpoint and historical navigation
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Retain parent-linked immutable snapshots and their captured source/artifact bytes. Historical inspection is a pure read. Restoring or branching state is an explicit authorized event with migration/compatibility checks, not overwriting journal history.
requirements.acceptance: Navigate an old checkpoint after new work; verify its original bytes and source references. An unsupported branch/restore operation advertises unsupported rather than a fake success.

requirements.title: Effects and delivery uncertainty
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Separate intent, dispatch, external acknowledgement and reconciliation for effectful tool calls. Use transactional outbox records and idempotent consumers where available. At-least-once delivery is normal; ambiguous external completion remains UNKNOWN until reconciled.
requirements.acceptance: Simulate a crash after dispatch but before acknowledgement; replay does not silently repeat an irreversible effect, and the uncertain receipt is visible.

requirements.title: Integrity checks and repair
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Verify genesis, chain, recorded reducer results, materialized state, artifact blobs and checkpoint links on reopen and on demand. Refuse to continue silently on corruption. Repair creates an explicitly authorized recovery lineage while preserving damaged evidence.
requirements.acceptance: Tests corrupt distinct storage layers and assert specific detection. Backup restoration is demonstrated from an independently retained copy.

requirements.title: Runtime resource bounds
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Enforce input sizes, graph/search depth, arithmetic bit limits, CPU/time/memory/disk and concurrency budgets at appropriate process boundaries. A Python counter is not a general operating-system sandbox. Long-running work renews declared leases and reports progress.
requirements.acceptance: Adversarial inputs hit typed budget outcomes; worker isolation and host resource controls are measured where external or native execution is admitted.

requirements.title: Observable service health
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Expose versioned state, event cursor, checkpoint head, verifier status, research pause, active work, blockers, current revision and capability limits. Liveness and readiness have distinct meanings. Read access never advances semantic state.
requirements.acceptance: Repeated GET calls leave the revision unchanged; readiness fails for unresolved integrity failure; disconnected clients see stale/unknown rather than fabricated live values.

requirements.title: Portable database and storage adaptation
requirements.title_group: Durable state machines and service kernel
requirements.mandate: Keep a documented logical schema and migration ledger. Benchmark whether PostgreSQL, graph projections and object storage improve the actual workload. Graph indexes are derived views of source/evidence records and cannot become untraceable alternative truth stores.
requirements.acceptance: A storage migration exports/imports a fixture and historical event chain with equal semantic state, retained blobs and recoverable source links.

requirements.title: Machine-operable discovery
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Publish a versioned discovery document naming only implemented read routes, command envelopes, authentication scopes, schemas, limits and continuation semantics. Stable URLs permit an independent agent to inspect the service without private narrative context.
requirements.acceptance: A clean API client discovers the service, reads state, follows a checkpoint and submits one authorized command using the published protocol alone.

requirements.title: Guidance receipt
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Each guidance item carries immutable identity, issuer, target, text, optional typed action, relevant source/obligation references and expected revision. Accepting guidance records receipt, not compliance or execution. Preserve the exact submitted text.
requirements.acceptance: The submit receipt returns guidance ID and revision; malformed or unauthorized submissions cannot appear as accepted guidance.

requirements.title: Explicit acknowledgement
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: An operator or harness explicitly acknowledges, defers or rejects guidance with reason and actor. Never infer acknowledgement from polling, elapsed time or a model's prose. Expose pending guidance prominently and retain all dispositions.
requirements.acceptance: A submit/ack lifecycle is visible from a second client; duplicate ack and invalid dispositions have deterministic documented behavior.

requirements.title: Applied guidance and actual effects
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Apply only an acknowledged typed action admitted by the command contract. Record the exact resulting changes and applied revision. Text-only advice may be acknowledged, but cannot be marked APPLIED until an implemented action or linked production fulfills it.
requirements.acceptance: Priority, pause and resume actions alter actual state; unsupported free-text execution is refused; receipts distinguish ACKNOWLEDGED from APPLIED.

requirements.title: Guidance visibility and collaboration
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Codex checks pending guidance at defined safe checkpoints and observes authenticated events while working. Two agents can independently inspect and guide the same commission with revision guards. A collaborator's changes must be visible to Codex before dependent execution continues.
requirements.acceptance: Two-client test demonstrates submission, detection, acknowledgement, application and conflict recovery without lost updates or covert state rewriting.

requirements.title: Production capture
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: PRODUCE captures actual artifact bytes, paths, versions and semantic scope. Preserve immutable snapshots even if a working file later changes. Show workspace drift separately, and require explicit re-production for a new candidate.
requirements.acceptance: Produce/reopen tests resolve the original bytes; editing the workspace does not alter captured evidence and cannot silently certify the changed file.

requirements.title: Verification execution
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: VERIFY invokes a registered trusted verifier with declared inputs, source identity and evidence class. The caller cannot supply a pass flag, substitute a hash-looking string or bypass scientific checks with file existence. A failed verifier remains visible and blocks acceptance.
requirements.acceptance: Forged evidence, unknown verifiers, tampered artifacts and explicit failing checks all refuse acceptance; successful receipts bind actual verifier code and inputs.

requirements.title: Acceptance and supersession
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: ACCEPT applies only to the verified artifact version and its exact obligations. Later production invalidates the candidate's previous verification while retaining historical accepted snapshots. Whole-mission acceptance is a separate conjunction of required gates.
requirements.acceptance: A re-produced artifact cannot inherit acceptance automatically; accepting the bootstrap cannot change the full mission to commissioned.

requirements.title: DODGE work contracts
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Every work item has Deliverable, Obligations, Dependencies, Guards and Evidence. This package's DODGE label is a house organizational convention. It links expected outputs and definitions of done without forcing Codex to follow arbitrary calendar phases.
requirements.acceptance: Machine registry validates all five fields, dependency references and evidence requirements; UI displays dependency-ready and blocked work intelligibly.

requirements.title: Refusal and diagnostic custody
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Retain refusal reason, attempted kind, actor scope, expected/current revision and safe diagnostics separately from accepted transitions. Redact credentials and private payloads according to policy. A refusal is useful evidence, not an unreported exception.
requirements.acceptance: Negative controls are queryable; authentication failures reveal no state or tokens; unsupported command paths have stable error codes.

requirements.title: Human-readable workbench
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Provide a real working interface for state, obligations, sources, produced artifacts, verification outcomes, guidance, experiments, checkpoints and blockers. Use actual service data, honest connection indicators and accessible controls. Keep implementation jargon out of explanations where it does not help a decision.
requirements.acceptance: A human can complete submit/ack/apply and produce/verify/accept workflows through the UI and see the same receipts as an API client.

requirements.title: Progress without narrative dependence
requirements.title_group: Guidance, produce/verify and the commission interface
requirements.mandate: Each checkpoint exports a concise STATUS, NEXT_STATE, source lock, capability index, obligation/evidence matrix, negative results and cost report. These are projections of machine state and immutable receipts, not independently edited claims of success.
requirements.acceptance: A new Codex or observer reconstructs completed, active and blocked work from the URL or repository export, with no need for the prior chat transcript.

requirements.title: Formal vocabulary
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Define symbol, token, letter, alphabet, word, expression, grammar, interpretation, value, type, operator, state, transition, machine, model, theorem and witness with distinct identities. Preserve source-specific senses through namespaces and aliases. The same spelling may name different mathematical structures.
requirements.acceptance: Vocabulary schema records established/house status, source anchors, examples and non-examples; ambiguous terms resolve to alternatives rather than silent conflation.

requirements.title: Typed alphabets
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: An alphabet is a declared family of typed generators with identity, admissibility and coordinates/relations where relevant. Support finite enumerations and effective generators, including lettered, numeric, geometric, graph-indexed, phonetic and product forms. An organizational table is an alphabet representation only under an explicit interpretation.
requirements.acceptance: Construct one validated alphabet of each inherited kind, demonstrate a product alphabet and distinguish a periodic-table layout from a chemical generative law.

requirements.title: Words and index structures
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Represent a word as a labeling of an explicit finite index structure: sequence, tuple, rooted tree, graph, grid, multiset or cyclic order. Keep index shape and symbol identities separate. State the symmetry/equivalence used to identify representations.
requirements.acceptance: Round trips preserve labeled structure; tests distinguish ordered tuples from multisets and graph incidence from a renderer's layout.

requirements.title: Grammar interface
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: A grammar declares alphabet/signature, admissible constructions, derivation relation, diagnostics, version and applicable decision procedure. Support regular, context-free, tree, graph, attribute and term-rewriting adapters with honest termination/decidability limits. Uniform interfaces do not establish a universal membership algorithm.
requirements.acceptance: Positive/negative fixtures cover each supported formalism, and unsupported or resource-limited membership returns an explicit non-proof result.

requirements.title: In-grammar and negative forms
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Store scoped prohibited, missing, conflicting, hypothetical and empirically excluded forms with provenance and evidence. In-grammar is not automatically the logical complement of a language and a dataset omission is not impossibility. Negative information participates in planning and explanation.
requirements.acceptance: Distinct fixtures produce no-edge-found, forbidden-by-rule, contradicted-by-witness, unresolved and budget-exhausted results without collapsing them.

requirements.title: Expression and evaluation
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Parse expressions into typed structure before interpretation. Distinguish syntax, denotation, evaluation strategy and execution effects. Explain f(g(x)), matrix transpose/product and chemical formulae through their declared environments; a short string may denote an expensive operation but is not executable without semantics.
requirements.acceptance: Tests validate function-composition order, matrix dimensions and a chemical formula's descriptive role; ambiguous or unbound symbols are refused with context.

requirements.title: Denotation and realization
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Every grammar declares a semantic domain and partial interpretation. Admissibility, realizability, computability and affordability are separate properties. H2O encodes composition under a chemical notation contract; it does not by itself specify preparation, geometry or a physical process.
requirements.acceptance: Produce examples of valid syntax with undefined denotation, an interpreted object with no admitted executor and a valid but budget-exceeding computation.

requirements.title: Equality and equivalence
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Name syntactic equality, canonical-form equality, structural isomorphism, observational equivalence and theorem-level equality separately. Finite numerical agreement is evidence on tested points only. Quotients declare their relation and assumptions before representatives are merged.
requirements.acceptance: Tests retain domain exclusions, detect a counterexample outside sampled points and prevent numerical support from being promoted to universal equality.

requirements.title: Types, contexts and assumptions
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Every operation carries type, algebraic context, units, domain restrictions, effects and evidence requirements. Context transport is a declared map with preservation/loss obligations. A changed context can yield the same result, so dependency custody cannot rely only on output inequality.
requirements.acceptance: Context-sensitive examples record both dependencies even when outputs coincide, and reject incompatible fields, dimensions or authorization contexts.

requirements.title: State and variance grammar
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Define state space, event alphabet, transition relation, guards, observations and invariant predicates. A state shift is a typed transition; an observation or rendering change has its own declared effect class. Study trace languages, bisimulation and compositional contracts without assuming every state system is finite.
requirements.acceptance: A machine's trace validates against its declared grammar; illegal shifts and semantic mutations disguised as view changes are detected.

requirements.title: Charts, transliteration and transport
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Generalize transliteration as a typed representation transport only after defining source/target alphabets, parsing, interpretation, loss and inverse relation. Keep phonetic transliteration, notation conversion, compilation and semantic analogy distinct even when they share a pipeline shape.
requirements.acceptance: Chart round trips preserve stated observables or return explicit ambiguity/loss, with one linguistic and one mathematical/software example.

requirements.title: Costs as structured semantics
requirements.title_group: Forms, alphabets, grammars and semantics
requirements.mandate: Record work, space, output size, build/index cost and effect cost relative to a model and input dimensions. O(2) is constant asymptotically; logarithmic and exponential claims require specified functions. Complexity classes and data-structure taxonomies may form alphabets with their own grammars but do not make runtime comparison automatic.
requirements.acceptance: Benchmarks state input size, model and overhead; a vocabulary test distinguishes O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n) and O(2^n) with correct examples.

requirements.title: Promotion object
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Promote a grammar or certified compositional path to a higher-level letter carrying immutable source identity, external type, interpretation, expansion map, evidence, cost and loss. The letter represents a structured object; it is not merely a new name pasted onto unverified behavior.
requirements.acceptance: A promoted grammar can be addressed, inspected, expanded and used in another validated grammar while retaining its original source and contracts.

requirements.title: Representation recovery
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Specify what expansion recovers: exact source bytes, canonical serialization, derivation tree or equivalence class. Retaining a pointer is insufficient unless the bytes remain retrievable. Preserve token boundaries and versioned encodings.
requirements.acceptance: Delete a working copy and recover the captured source from the package/store; compare the promised bytes or canonical representation exactly.

requirements.title: Semantic preservation
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Supply a separate preservation obligation for promoted objects under stated denotation or observations. Lossless syntactic expansion does not imply semantic equivalence across every context. Finite exhaustive checks and formal proofs have different scopes and labels.
requirements.acceptance: A finite promotion checks every member of its declared finite language; a broader promotion records its proof or remains proposed with an explicit unproved obligation.

requirements.title: Lossy folds and quotients
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: A many-to-one promotion declares discarded distinctions, quotient relation and questions no longer answerable. Keep side information when exact recovery is required. Never describe a lossy quotient as globally reversible merely because one representative is stored.
requirements.acceptance: A noninjective counterexample demonstrates ambiguity, and a side-data round trip recovers the original where the contract promises it.

requirements.title: Explicate, implicate and complicate
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Preserve Plicastratum's named operations and source-specific meanings. Implement expansion/analysis, folding/encapsulation and composed unfolding as versioned operators with domains, invariants and failure states. Avoid substituting intuitive prose for executable laws.
requirements.acceptance: At least one source-grounded operator per named operation has fixtures, a negative case and a relation to the original definition.

requirements.title: Promotion tower and identity depth
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Represent successive alphabets and their maps as a typed tower. Track identity at representation, state, declared holonomy and chain levels where defined. Seven strata, seven-complete terminology and University division numbers are separate namespaces.
requirements.acceptance: A multi-level tower expands to its base representation, reports each preserved/lost property and resolves overloaded terminology without numerical conflation.

requirements.title: Trace mining
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Mine repeated admitted trace segments as candidate higher operators. Preserve ordering, parameterization, preconditions, effects and costs. Frequency suggests reuse; it does not prove semantic equivalence or correctness.
requirements.acceptance: Mine a repeated trace, propose a macro, verify it against its expansion on declared cases and retain a counterexample for an invalid macro.

requirements.title: Structural canonicalization
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Declare normalization rules, symmetry actions and representative selection. Check confluence/termination where claimed, or expose order dependence and finite bounds. Stable content IDs use domain-separated canonical encodings.
requirements.acceptance: Isomorphic representations canonicalize under the promised action, nonisomorphic controls remain distinct, and normalization claims are scoped to tested/proved domains.

requirements.title: Operator alphabets
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Treat operations, data structures, algorithms, types and complexity descriptors as typed alphabet citizens. A grammar over them specifies valid compositions, policies and cost constraints. Keep implementation choices separate from mathematical denotations.
requirements.acceptance: Construct a valid algorithm/data-structure composition and reject an incompatible one, with resulting cost model and witness obligations.

requirements.title: Alphabets of grammars
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Support higher grammars whose letters are complete lower grammars with independent namespaces and contracts. Composition declares how lower-language variables, symbols and interpretations align. Resolve collisions explicitly and allow multi-input grammar constructors.
requirements.acceptance: Compose two independently versioned grammars into a higher language; inspect both expansions, reject a namespace/type collision and explain the resulting interpretation.

requirements.title: Promotion admission and invalidation
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: A candidate promotion becomes reusable only after its declared verification and packaging gates. Changed dependency semantics require a new promotion version and dependent revalidation. Old expansions and receipts remain available.
requirements.acceptance: Replace one dependency and show impacted promotions lose current eligibility while historical certified versions still resolve.

requirements.title: Tower discovery agenda
requirements.title_group: Grammar-as-letter promotion and constructive towers
requirements.mandate: Treat new grammar-letter structures as research hypotheses with measurable utility: compression, reuse, interpretation preservation, search cost and explanatory power. Enumerate bounded candidates and counterexamples instead of promising unlimited automatic discovery.
requirements.acceptance: A reproducible experiment compares promoted and unpromoted representations, including overhead, losses, failure cases and an explicit continuation frontier.

requirements.title: Q-String identity
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Preserve the source Q-String record as a classical typed computational relation carrying provenance, context, grammar, evidence and version. Quantum is a house metaphor unless a separate physical model supplies actual quantum states and operations. A verified-looking status string grants no execution authority.
requirements.acceptance: Schema/admission tests reject relations missing type/context/evidence and distinguish descriptive records from executable admitted operators.

requirements.title: Relation before uniqueness
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Represent one-to-many and many-to-many relations before imposing a function. Preserve competing outputs and source disagreements; uniqueness is a separately witnessed property on a declared domain.
requirements.acceptance: Reverse lookup returns a candidate set with sources, and an attempted unjustified functional coercion is refused.

requirements.title: Typed directed hypergraph
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Use named/ordered input and output ports with incidence, types, constraints, context, provenance and time/version. An n-ary operation is one joint hyperedge, not independent unary arcs. Maintain DK0 and EFC source meanings through adapters.
requirements.acceptance: A two-input rule cannot fire when only one premise is reachable; swapped noncommutative ports and incorrect multiplicity are detected.

requirements.title: Q-path composition
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: A Q-path composes admissible hyperedges with explicit bindings, context transport, invariant/loss composition and witness aggregation. Record all premises and outputs. Composition legality and the truth of external claims remain separate checks.
requirements.acceptance: Execute a multi-step, multi-input path and reconstruct each port binding; reject missing, wrong-type or wrong-context prerequisites.

requirements.title: Reachability semantics
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Define reachable relative to registered operators, available premises, context, authority and finite resource policy. Fully reachable means addressable/searchable under supported contracts, not that every node has a valid edge to every other node or that every problem is decidable.
requirements.acceptance: Search returns found, disproved-under-complete-finite-search, unknown, blocked and resource-limit with reasons and the exact explored boundary.

requirements.title: Context and witness transport
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: A relation preserves only the invariants it declares. Compose source witnesses and expose missing obligations rather than reusing evidence from incompatible contexts. Changes in policy, algebra or units can invalidate a path even when identifiers look similar.
requirements.acceptance: A context change triggers revalidation; a compatible transport has a preservation receipt, while missing transports remain unsupported.

requirements.title: Multicategorical composition
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Treat multiple-input operators and their substitution as typed multimorphisms where the laws actually hold. Declare associativity, identities, symmetry and effects. Noncommutative or effectful composition retains ordering and cannot inherit symmetric laws automatically.
requirements.acceptance: Compare two legal bracketings under stated assumptions, and demonstrate a counterexample to swapping effectful or ordered inputs.

requirements.title: Costs and path planning
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Plan under typed admissibility and explicit cost vectors before heuristic ranking. Keep latency, memory, evidence strength, information loss and effect budgets distinct. A cheaper path is not necessarily more correct or more source-faithful.
requirements.acceptance: Competing admissible paths produce a justified Pareto/selected result under a versioned policy, and an invalid low-cost path is rejected.

requirements.title: Relation kinds and negative edges
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Distinguish implication, analogy, structural isomorphism, representation transport, empirical association, translation, borrowing, causality and policy refusal. A named edge never silently changes kind during composition.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-domain examples show which edge kinds compose and which do not; unsupported causal or semantic conclusions are blocked.

requirements.title: Higher structures with hypotheses
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Distinguish graph cycles, algebraic rings, simplicial nerves, fundamental groups, sheaves and holonomy. Construct them only from the required data and hypotheses; a visual loop is not evidence of every corresponding structure.
requirements.acceptance: Nerve/sheaf examples provide intersections or restriction maps and compatibility checks; insufficient input yields a specific missing-hypothesis result.

requirements.title: Q-path packages and replay
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Package a path with signatures, dependency versions, contexts, source witnesses, cost policy, trace and revalidation procedure. Provide a pure inspection projection and a separately admitted execution interface.
requirements.acceptance: Export/import a path, replay its recorded result and execute a new reproduction; historical and current runs have distinct identities.

requirements.title: Relational opportunity discovery
requirements.title_group: Q-Strings, typed Q-paths and joint composition
requirements.mandate: Identify absent adapters, inconsistent relations, reusable subpaths and cross-domain candidate laws as research opportunities. Each proposal names its baseline, unsupported step, falsifiable test and expected benefit.
requirements.acceptance: The system emits an opportunity from a bounded graph gap with linked evidence and a runnable experiment proposal, without presenting the proposed relation as established.

requirements.title: Native source language
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Deliver a documented native language with lexer, parser, typed AST and intermediate representation. Preserve the original PolyIA native-language obligation. JSON serves APIs, registries and evidence; the bootstrap command envelope is not claimed to replace a scientific native grammar.
requirements.acceptance: Parse and compile meaningful source programs, show type errors at source spans, and compare generated execution with an independently checked expected result.

requirements.title: Intermediate representation
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Define PIR and subject IRs with explicit types, contexts, assumptions, dependencies, effects, costs, source spans and proof obligations. Lowering preserves stated semantics or records loss. Do not equate a textual plan with executable code.
requirements.acceptance: Round-trip IR serialization and verify at least one linguistic and one nonlinguistic lowering through the same core contract.

requirements.title: Independent computational atoms
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Each atom declares public ports, state lifecycle, version, external semantics, witnesses and budgets. It is independently buildable, testable, replaceable and observable. Size does not determine independence; enforce no undeclared implementation coupling.
requirements.acceptance: Install an atom in isolation and substitute a compatible implementation without importing its private internals or silently changing behavior.

requirements.title: Typed module resolution
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Resolve providers by type, version, capabilities and constraints. Enumerate ambiguity rather than silently selecting a similarly named library. ABI incompatibility and missing grants are compilation failures with actionable diagnostics.
requirements.acceptance: Positive and negative provider-resolution fixtures cover multiple providers, wrong versions, unavailable tools and incompatible ABI.

requirements.title: SDK and package construction
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Generate specialized SDKs and software packages from admitted compositions through partial evaluation and explicit dependency closure. Avoid bundling every project merely to claim reuse. Keep classes, objects, protocols and language bindings as separate realizations of a common contract.
requirements.acceptance: A generated package executes from a clean environment with only declared dependencies and includes its source/evidence manifest.

requirements.title: Tool contract schema
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Every tool declares input/output schemas, preconditions, effect class, data reads, authority scope, limits, timeout, idempotency behavior, cancellation and result/evidence schema. Curl-like network access is an explicit tool, not ambient power granted to all generators.
requirements.acceptance: A contract validator and broker reject invalid input, ungranted effects and oversized outputs; successful calls retain actual tool version and receipts.

requirements.title: Tool broker and isolation
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Invoke tools only through an admitted broker. Pure kernels, local storage, network readers, mutators and unsafe native plugins have different capability profiles. Use OS/process isolation where required and minimize ephemeral memory scopes without claiming that scoped variables form a sandbox.
requirements.acceptance: Denied filesystem/network/process operations fail in an isolation test; the broker records dispatch, timeout/cancellation and output custody.

requirements.title: Generator and witness roles
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Declare constructor, normalizer, filter, oracle/witness and renderer roles separately. Native generation cannot secretly read sealed witness answers. A library used during construction must be declared as part of construction and cannot be presented as an independent post-seal witness for the same claim.
requirements.acceptance: Role/import/read audits detect witness leakage and the inherited RDKit-role mismatch; revised experiments identify dependencies and independent checks honestly.

requirements.title: Execution admission
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Generated code, plans, grammar paths and model proposals remain untrusted candidate artifacts until type, effect, resource and verification gates admit them. A corpus executable flag or hash alone cannot authorize running it.
requirements.acceptance: Attempts to run unregistered handlers, eval strings or source-embedded commands are rejected; admitted code resolves to a specific verified package version.

requirements.title: Language-neutral interfaces
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Use stable schemas and IDL/WIT where supported. Provide real tested Python and JavaScript/TypeScript adapters first, then native/WASM bindings when tooling is present. Record unsupported hosts rather than shipping fabricated successful stubs.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-language contract tests exercise the same state command and scientific operation, including refusal behavior and version mismatch.

requirements.title: Model tool use as a client contract
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Examine Hermes, OpenCode and the intended OpenCLAR/OpenClaw reference using official current sources. Extract their tool-call schema/broker ideas where useful. Keep language models, coding agents and orchestration tools distinct; unresolved product identity remains explicit.
requirements.acceptance: An architecture comparison cites exact versions and maps transferable mechanisms to PolyIA contracts; the required no-LLM path passes with every optional model adapter disabled.

requirements.title: Effects, memory and protocols
requirements.title_group: Native compilation, software units and tool contracts
requirements.mandate: Model filesystem, database, network and persistent-state effects explicitly in software/state-machine contracts. Ephemeral workspaces have scoped lifetimes and cleanup receipts. Protocol evolutions preserve command compatibility or require negotiated versions and migrations.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover resource cleanup, incompatible protocol versions, cancellation and external-effect uncertainty without losing the associated evidence.

requirements.title: Constructive generation
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: A generator produces objects from declared primitives and rules, with derivation traces and bounded search. Distinguish generation, recognition, retrieval, interpolation and unconstrained proposal. A retrieved example is not evidence that a generative law produced it.
requirements.acceptance: Generate a previously unlisted admissible object under a finite contract and retain a replayable derivation plus an independent checker result.

requirements.title: Generative model contract
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Define each model by input/output types, parameters/state, generation law, constraints, declared reads, randomness, evidence and costs. A model need not be an LLM or a neural network. Store learned parameters separately from grammar rules and runtime policy.
requirements.acceptance: Model schema validates grammar-based, probabilistic and optional neural instances with distinct capabilities and no hidden inference dependency.

requirements.title: Non-LLM language generation
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Implement a useful bounded example using finite-state transduction, typed templates, morphology and/or a probabilistic grammar. Generate terminology-aware explanations with source references and explicit supported intent coverage. Do not promise arbitrary open-domain comprehension from the existence of a state machine.
requirements.acceptance: Produce different valid tones/representations from one verified content plan, preserve every factual relation and reject unsupported requested claims.

requirements.title: State-map accompaniment
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Package generative models with a state-map controller that tracks accepted input, candidate generation, constraints, verification, representation choices, tool calls and refusal. The map provides inspectable search and workflow structure; it is not infinite memory or unlimited semantic understanding.
requirements.acceptance: Inspect and replay a model's state trace, change an admitted style choice and observe output variation without changing certified content.

requirements.title: Optional narrow neural models
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Permit pretrained non-LLM speech, acoustic, ranking, recognition or other narrow models only as declared optional components with version, license, inputs, measured behavior and resource costs. Determine whether a chosen component contains an LLM rather than assuming its product label.
requirements.acceptance: Compare a narrow model with the deterministic baseline, including errors and latency; disabling it preserves every core acceptance workflow.

requirements.title: Constraint-driven model construction
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Compile a problem's typed grammar, state map, available tools and verified operations into a specialized generator. Program specialization may be fast without retraining weights. A new model package needs its own boundaries, acceptance and identity.
requirements.acceptance: Given a supported commission, emit an independently executable model/package with source lock, constraints and tests, then run it in a clean environment.

requirements.title: Randomness and reproducibility
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Declare deterministic and stochastic components. Record seed, algorithm, distribution, dependency version and sampling budget. Reproducibility of a sampled run is distinct from statistical validity or exhaustive coverage.
requirements.acceptance: Reproduce fixed-seed outputs and run a separate distributional evaluation with denominators and uncertainty; no random result is labeled proof merely because it repeats.

requirements.title: Inverse and relational generation
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Generate preimages or candidate explanations as a relation with domain, search policy, uniqueness status and witness obligations. Separate no preimage under a proved finite domain from not found under a budget.
requirements.acceptance: Inverse fixtures include unique, multiple, impossible-in-declared-domain and unresolved cases with source and counterexample records.

requirements.title: Curriculum and explanation generation
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Generate learning sequences from formal prerequisites, source coverage and tested examples. Explanations retain assumptions, notation translations and evidence grades. The user can move from elementary fractions through polynomial division to derivative rules without losing the distinctions between them.
requirements.acceptance: A curriculum path identifies prerequisites and derives the polynomial/product/quotient connection using actual calculations and inspectable source-linked steps.

requirements.title: Machine and package synthesis
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Synthesize state machines, APIs, protocols, classes or SDKs only within registered constructive families. Every production carries an executable behavior contract, interface dependencies and verification plan. General program synthesis remains a research frontier with decidability and cost limits.
requirements.acceptance: Synthesize two distinct runnable packages under bounded grammar families, check their contracts and retain a failed synthesis with a precise unsupported/budget result.

requirements.title: Optimization without semantic drift
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Search for transformations that improve declared metrics while preserving required observations, effects and source custody. Keep baseline and candidate results separate. A syntactically shorter or faster output may violate other constraints.
requirements.acceptance: An optimization experiment includes semantic regression, adverse cases, total production cost and a measured improvement threshold before admission.

requirements.title: Generative frontier governance
requirements.title_group: Constructive generation and state-map models
requirements.mandate: Continuously enumerate supported experiment opportunities under budgets and standing authority. Track explored regions, equivalent candidates, promising gaps and counterexamples. Do not equate a running loop with productive discovery.
requirements.acceptance: The worker records generated, duplicate, refused, tested and admitted counts, plus resource use and meaningful stop/pause conditions.

requirements.title: Mathematics coverage atlas
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Register canonical University subjects and conventional mathematical fields, using versioned external taxonomies as navigation aids. Include logic, sets, algebra, analysis, geometry, topology, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, number theory and applied mathematics. Taxonomic inclusion does not assert implementation.
requirements.acceptance: A complete topic inventory preserves existing IDs and maps every inherited mathematics obligation to its capability/evidence state and further dependencies.

requirements.title: Computer science coverage atlas
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Include computability, languages, automata, algorithms, complexity, data structures, programming languages, type systems, compilers, databases, distributed systems, software design and learning methods. Model their structural and operational relations rather than grouping by names alone.
requirements.acceptance: Each inherited CS topic has source-linked operators or an explicit research gap; compare at least one algorithm/data-structure/cost combination through a typed path.

requirements.title: Exact arithmetic and polynomial forms
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Implement integer/rational arithmetic, field-scoped polynomial division, factorization under declared supported algorithms and rational-function domain guards. Distinguish Euclidean quotient/remainder from fractional division and derivative quotient rules while deriving their legitimate connection.
requirements.acceptance: For supplied a,b in K[x], certify a=bq+r and the remainder bound; compare product-rule and quotient-rule derivatives on b(x) nonzero and retain cancellation exclusions.

requirements.title: Calculus and integration methods
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Preserve term grammars, differentiation, higher-derivative orbit analysis, Leibniz/Faa di Bruno patterns, limits, series, integration-method machines and the Liouville/nonelementarity boundary. A failed integration search is not a proof of no elementary antiderivative.
requirements.acceptance: Each supported method has domain-aware positive/negative cases and a derivative witness; unsupported elementary/non-elementary classification remains explicit.

requirements.title: Linear algebra and algebraic structures
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Support typed matrices, composition, systems, decompositions, linear maps, groups, rings and fields under stated domains. Separate a matrix display from the computation it denotes. Preserve construction gaps and distinguish split extensions from non-split ones accurately.
requirements.acceptance: Dimension/type checks, exact residuals and structure laws validate examples; the inherited A4/non-split claim is corrected with the original preserved.

requirements.title: Topology and relational structure
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Preserve simplicial complexes, finite homology, Euler characteristic, scoped fundamental group presentations and topologies of forms/worlds. State coefficient fields and what invariants can or cannot classify. Do not infer integral torsion or complete homeomorphism classification from rational/F2 ranks.
requirements.acceptance: Boundary-squared tests and independently checked examples identify coefficient choices, limitations and relevant source amendments.

requirements.title: Numerical mathematics
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Treat ODE solvers, Runge–Kutta/Butcher trees, phase portraits, numerical integration, error and stability as machines with method-specific assumptions and tolerances. Separate rounding, discretization, sampling and model errors.
requirements.acceptance: A reproducible solver comparison includes convergence/error checks, stability limits, step policy, failures and actual cost measurements.

requirements.title: Chemistry alphabet and grammar
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Preserve UCG's element, orbital, valence, compound, molecule, nomenclature, symmetry, stereochemistry and stoichiometry obligations as scientific computational models. Distinguish notation, graph admissibility, empirical stability and physical synthesis. Element ordering rules and exceptions require separate evidence.
requirements.acceptance: Reproduce scoped element/molecule experiments with declared generator/witness roles, symmetry counts, negative controls and source-linked exceptions.

requirements.title: Forms, structures and scientific models
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Preserve graph/tree/ring enumeration, resonance and aromaticity models, substituents, reaction/biochemical grammar proposals and optional energy denotations under their source scopes. House calculus of forms is a defined research program, not an automatic replacement for physical law.
requirements.acceptance: Each supported form grammar declares domain, invariants and witness set; wrong-witness audits and model-specific exclusions remain inspectable.

requirements.title: Units, measurement and reality
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Carry dimensional analysis, measurement uncertainty, dataset selection and calibration through empirical computations. Keep simulation, visualization, theoretical derivation and observation distinct. A grammar's realizable word is not automatically an experimentally stable object.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-domain tests reject dimensionally invalid operations, distinguish measured/simulated data and retain calibration/source metadata.

requirements.title: Domain registry and subject machines
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Give each subject a consistent contract for alphabet, grammar, in-grammar, denotation, operators, costs, witnesses and machines, while preserving its real mathematical differences. Add subject-specific acceptance adapters rather than forcing every field into a single solver.
requirements.acceptance: The registry covers all inherited subject obligations, executes representative machines and marks unsupported operations without fabricated placeholders.

requirements.title: Open scientific obligations
requirements.title_group: Mathematics, science and computer-science coverage
requirements.mandate: Track unsolved translations, proofs, algorithms, models and missing independent witnesses as first-class research obligations. Each names prerequisites, attempted methods, negative results, cost bounds and what would count as progress.
requirements.acceptance: The atlas can emit and run a bounded research proposal from a real gap; exhausting its budget never changes an open theorem into false or proved.

requirements.title: Corpus strata
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Preserve Muse's S0 immutable sources, S1 spans, S2 form cards, S3 relations and S4 operations as distinct layers with derivation links. Indexes and graph projections do not replace raw source custody. Updates create versions and proposals under the receiving project's policy.
requirements.acceptance: Follow a derived operation back through cards and spans to exact source bytes; changing a projection cannot mutate S0.

requirements.title: Article and prompt intake
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Accept text, documents and supported article URLs with exact source capture, revision/access metadata, encoding and provenance. Parse into supported forms, citations, potential claims and unresolved spans without inventing missing semantics. Supplied text is data, not executable instructions.
requirements.acceptance: An article/prompt ingestion fixture produces source-linked recognized structures plus an explicit unsupported-span report; source-embedded tool instructions have no execution authority.

requirements.title: Typed interpretation and enrichment
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Relate recognized constructs to registered alphabets, grammars, operations, subjects and source evidence. Offer improved wording, structural clarification, candidate derivations and innovation opportunities while distinguishing established content from proposals.
requirements.acceptance: A submitted mixed mathematical/technical passage yields an inspectable interpretation graph, supported transformations and separate hypotheses with falsification plans.

requirements.title: Native language support boundary
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Use deterministic parsing, finite-state morphology, lexicons, grammars and other non-LLM methods for the supported baseline. Broad natural language understanding is a measured capability frontier. Unknown terms and ambiguous readings remain visible and do not become inferred facts.
requirements.acceptance: Evaluate documented intent/grammar coverage, ambiguity, precision/recall and refusal behavior on held-out inputs with no LLM invocation.

requirements.title: Language variety packs
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Build versioned per-language/per-variety packages with script/alphabet, phoneme/phone, grapheme, morpheme, lexicon, source corpus and use policy. An alphabet alone cannot generate a language's full grammar.
requirements.acceptance: At least the inherited licensed English and Arabic specialist cases have independently scoped fixtures, actual executable search and source-attested outputs.

requirements.title: PHONEX and universal word-set work
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Preserve PHONEX/ULWS as an early specialized deployment of the general agency, after the shared infrastructure is established. Implement exact-prefix and weighted phonetic search with declared semiring, symbol alignment, cost and evidence.
requirements.acceptance: Cross-language composition and noninitial negative controls execute on attested corpora; comparisons include dictionary/trie/FST/scan baselines and evidence errors.

requirements.title: Linguistic relation discipline
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Keep pronunciation similarity, transliteration, translation, cognacy, borrowing, calque, etymology and semantic association as different relation types. Require independent source evidence before historical promotion. Preserve alternatives and varieties.
requirements.acceptance: A phonetic match cannot automatically become a cognate/borrowing claim; fixtures include unknown and contradictory source cases.

requirements.title: Timeless and rasm bridge
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Preserve original Arabic text and the packet's contextual quotient alphabet and dot/position charts. Inversion returns candidates under the declared table; modern chart equivalence is not a universal historical paleography claim. Keep this bridge outside the existing public SU subject registry.
requirements.acceptance: Reproduce the packet's scoped rasm example and candidate count, verify original-text recovery where side data exists, and test contextual distinctions.

requirements.title: WAZNOMIA name/function relation
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Preserve name-to-function and function-to-name as partial set-valued relations with witnesses, source scope and loss. Formal nomenclature can be executable under a declared grammar; arbitrary natural-language names do not thereby become trustworthy programs.
requirements.acceptance: Both directions produce supported candidates, ambiguity and no-supported-result outcomes; unsupported etymologies are not synthesized as facts.

requirements.title: Greek and Latin determinations
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Apply the supplied morphology/nomenclature rules with source custody and a distinction between forms, historical transmission and modern technical convention. Borrowing, calque and unknown are valid outputs. Do not claim a parser exists where the source supplies only a research specification.
requirements.acceptance: Implemented parser scope is documented and tested on positive, negative and ambiguous examples; gaps remain explicit scientific obligations.

requirements.title: Cross-script and notation transport
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Build reversible or loss-declared transports among scripts, phonetic forms, mathematical notation, machine IR and accessible explanations. Keep exact source spelling alongside normalization. Different transport kinds share infrastructure but retain their own semantic requirements.
requirements.acceptance: At least one language transport and one mathematical notation transport preserve stated invariants and expose ambiguity/loss to human and API clients.

requirements.title: Corpus growth and privacy
requirements.title_group: Corpus, languages, nomenclature and source intake
requirements.mandate: Ingest new sources with deduplication, rights metadata, span custody and provenance. Separate private content from public exports and preserve authorized access constraints. A new article may propose a grammar relation, but admission waits for tests and evidence.
requirements.acceptance: A corpus update creates new versions and opportunities, respects export policy and cannot silently promote a proposed relation to established knowledge.

requirements.title: Experiment lifecycle
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Use a declared lifecycle including propose, generate, seal, witness, recognize, account, verify and checkpoint as appropriate. Preserve UCG's seal-before-witness principle. Experimental results include failures, unknowns and counterexamples, not only successes.
requirements.acceptance: Event history shows generator output sealed before the independent witness is accessed; illegal sequencing is refused.

requirements.title: Enforced read declarations
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: A generator's permitted inputs and witness separation must be enforced by the tool/process boundary rather than documentation alone. Include dataset/version identities, filesystem grants and hidden-state controls.
