requirements.acceptance: A deliberately witness-reading generator is blocked, and the receipt names the denied resource without exposing protected content.

requirements.title: Evidence identity and independence
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: A witness records method, assumptions, implementation provenance, inputs, outputs and independence relationship. Recomputing with the same implementation is self-consistency; genuinely independent baselines have separately identified methods or code.
requirements.acceptance: Evidence registry distinguishes self-check, differential check, exact finite check and proof; a claimed independent witness sharing the same oracle is flagged.

requirements.title: Exact and symbolic proof scope
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Use exact arithmetic or proof certificates for supported finite/algebraic claims; formal proofs include complete hypotheses and trusted-kernel information. Symbolic simplification carries domains. Numerical agreement cannot discharge a universal symbolic obligation.
requirements.acceptance: Known domain/cancellation and vacuous-sampling counterexamples fail the wrong verifier and pass only the appropriate scoped check.

requirements.title: Empirical and statistical evaluation
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Report dataset composition, denominators, sampling, train/held-out separation, precision, recall, error types, uncertainty and negative controls. A witness-derived amendment is labeled witness-informed and assessed on independent held-out cases.
requirements.acceptance: An experiment's metrics can be recalculated from retained outputs and witnesses, including its misses and contradictions.

requirements.title: Witness disagreement and audits
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Audit both the generator and witness when they disagree. Version corrected witness models and retain earlier results with their original scope. A benchmark dataset does not define universal possibility.
requirements.acceptance: Reproduce a documented wrong-witness case, publish the correction and re-evaluate affected claims without rewriting history.

requirements.title: Continuous worker
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Run a supervised bounded worker on the target VM with queues, leases, checkpoints, budgets, pause/resume and failure backoff. Persist progress across restarts. The package's finite demonstration worker is a seed, not evidence of indefinite production operation.
requirements.acceptance: A deployed worker survives restart, obeys pause and quotas, avoids duplicate admission and records measured activity over a declared observation period.

requirements.title: Experiment proposal generation
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Derive candidate experiments from typed graph gaps, grammar deficits, failed inverses, repeated traces and benchmark regressions. Each proposal names baseline, hypothesis, variation space, witness, budget and admission criterion.
requirements.acceptance: Generate a proposal from an actual recorded gap and execute its bounded design, preserving both promising and failed outcomes.

requirements.title: Reproduction and regression
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Pin source, code, dependencies, configuration and seeds. Reproduce separately from journal replay, then run regressions for affected capability families. Avoid broad unmotivated testing; target concrete risk and mandatory gates.
requirements.acceptance: A clean checkout reproduces selected results and executes scoped negative controls; a changed dependency produces a new run/version comparison.

requirements.title: Cost and performance evidence
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Measure cold/warm latency, quantiles, throughput, build and index cost, memory, storage and total package production cost under documented hardware and sample counts. Include cases where provenance or compilation costs make PolyIA slower.
requirements.acceptance: Benchmark reports compare fair baselines with fixed fixtures and explicitly state overhead, uncertainty and unsupported performance claims.

requirements.title: Counterexample and negative-result registry
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Keep immutable counterexamples, failed candidates, exhausted searches and contradictory witnesses with version scope and review response. Negative results improve grammar boundaries without automatic universalization.
requirements.acceptance: A prior counterexample remains queryable after a corrected release and prevents re-admitting the same invalid transformation.

requirements.title: Experiment acceptance record
requirements.title_group: Experiments, evidence and continuous inquiry
requirements.mandate: Completion of an experiment requires produced outputs, sealed inputs, actual witness receipts, verifier results and accounting. Formatting a valid JSON document or SHA-like string is insufficient. A successful experiment's evidence class is displayed everywhere it is reused.
requirements.acceptance: Tampered, missing, stale and caller-fabricated receipts fail admission; accepted experiments resolve to actual bytes and scoped scientific claims.

requirements.title: Candidate lifecycle
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Improvements move through proposal, implementation, verification, comparison, admission, activation and monitored operation. Keep research proposals separate from installed capability versions. Continuous learning means controlled capability evolution, not an unsupported claim of magically improving model weights.
requirements.acceptance: A candidate progresses only with required evidence, and a rejected candidate cannot become active through a status-field edit.

requirements.title: Version identity
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Assign immutable versions to grammar, alphabet, operator, model, state schema, compiler, tool contract, dataset and package. Record dependency locks and supersession edges. Human-friendly names resolve through explicit versions or a versioned selection policy.
requirements.acceptance: Historical clients resolve the original implementation after a newer version is active; ambiguous unpinned resolution is rejected or explicitly policy-selected.

requirements.title: Improvement thresholds
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Define baseline, metrics, tolerances, regression obligations and resource policy before evaluation. Improvement may trade speed, accuracy, coverage, interpretability and storage; retain the multidimensional result. Do not automatically supersede a trusted component on one favorable benchmark.
requirements.acceptance: A candidate that improves latency but breaks semantics fails admission; a documented tradeoff requires the authorized selection policy.

requirements.title: Impact analysis
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Trace dependent grammars, Q-paths, SDKs, source claims and state machines affected by a changed contract. Revalidate impacted boundaries and preserve unaffected historical evidence with its original version scope.
requirements.acceptance: Modify a low-level atom and show the exact affected dependency closure, required rechecks and still-valid independent packages.

requirements.title: Activation epoch and rollback
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Activate admitted releases through explicit state transitions binding package digest, policy, compatible state migration and previous epoch. Rollback restores a compatible retained release and accounts for irreversible external effects separately.
requirements.acceptance: Rehearse activation and rollback with a fixture, verify version selection and document any state/effect that cannot be undone.

requirements.title: Modular packaging
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Organize cohesive independently testable packages with declared ownership and public interfaces. Shared infrastructure serves all divisions; VII/VIII research does not monopolize the harness, packaging or verification services. Avoid a miscellaneous shared-utilities dependency sink.
requirements.acceptance: Dependency graph and isolated installation tests demonstrate replacement, source custody and absence of undeclared private imports.

requirements.title: Package manifests and custody
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Every package includes version, sources, licenses, build instructions, dependency lock, types/effects, evidence, limits and migration information. Preserve original authorship and modification history. A content hash identifies bytes but does not imply a license grant or truth.
requirements.acceptance: Manifest verification checks actual bytes and dependencies; redistribution/export applies declared rights and policy.

requirements.title: Compatibility and migration
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Publish schema/API compatibility rules and tested migrations. Database and event schema upgrades keep historical records readable by retained decoders. A new verifier version cannot silently rewrite an old receipt's meaning.
requirements.acceptance: Upgrade a stored fixture, verify old event decoding and semantic state, and reject an incompatible client with actionable diagnostics.

requirements.title: Research branches and release boundaries
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Keep candidate implementation branches, source archives and admitted runtime packages distinct. Isolate experiments from active service state and source repositories. Changes to shared work are reviewed against their contracts before activation.
requirements.acceptance: An experiment crash or invalid code candidate cannot mutate the active package or original source snapshot.

requirements.title: Reusable agency factory
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Make specialized agents/machines composable from admitted atoms and grammars. The concierge returns machine, IR, interfaces, dependencies, refusals, witnesses and human projection. A specialized language engine is one deployment of this common factory.
requirements.acceptance: Recompose the same kernel into one language specialist and one non-language computational service, each independently installable and verifiable.

requirements.title: Release evidence and limitations
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Publish actual tests, command results, environment, package hashes, benchmark scope, unsupported capabilities and residual risks. Historical reported tests are labeled separately from fresh release verification. Document meaningful limits without burying the working result.
requirements.acceptance: Release checker resolves every claimed fresh test to a real log/receipt and rejects claims based solely on inherited reports or planned commands.

requirements.title: Evolution science charter
requirements.title_group: Versioned improvement, modularity and package evolution
requirements.mandate: Use VII/VIII to investigate synthesis and evidence-governed evolution as research subjects, with falsifiable questions and comparative methods. Infrastructure improvement and scientific discovery are related but separate outcomes.
requirements.acceptance: Each charter has research objects, methods, open questions, measurable milestones, relation to I–VI/IX and publication criteria beyond merely shipping a service.

requirements.title: Astra identity and sources
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Integrate the recovered ASTRA Universal Traversals/Celestial Shells packet under its exact version and source contracts. Preserve Astra separately from ASTRO analytic scenes and the Astro web framework. Reuse actual code/contracts where verified rather than inventing a parallel meaning for the name.
requirements.acceptance: Adapter manifest pins the packet and maps every claimed capability to real files, existing API/report fields and independently assessed limitations.

requirements.title: ATOM transition adaptation
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Ground the adapter in a=(I,O,Q,delta,g,e,w,c): inputs, outputs, state, transition, guard, effects, witness and cost. Preserve OBSERVE, PROPOSE, ADMIT, EXECUTE, VERIFY, CHECKPOINT and HOLD semantics. Models may propose; atoms execute under guards.
requirements.acceptance: An actual ATOM-compatible operation maps to a PolyIA command/event and back to a state report without bypassing admission or verification.

requirements.title: Machine state versus render state
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Keep durable semantic state, view/camera state, animation frames and transient input separate. Read-only gestures and rendering do not become semantic mutations. An explicitly persistent view preference has its own effect contract.
requirements.acceptance: Camera movement leaves scientific/commission state unchanged; an admitted semantic command changes it and produces a durable receipt.

requirements.title: Astra geometry contract
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Preserve right-ascension/declination conversion to unit vectors, camera yaw/pitch and perspective projection with near-plane checks under stated units/conventions. Shell radii are authored display scales. Nearest-neighbor edges and visual closeness do not establish astronomical or semantic truth.
requirements.acceptance: Tests check vector norms, coordinate conventions, clipping and representative projections; synthetic/canonical catalog points and illustrative shells are labeled.

requirements.title: Function-space integration
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Use Astra to display typed mathematical structures, function operations and relations through declared geometry maps. Euclidean representation is a chosen projection; not every source space is Euclidean or faithfully embeddable without loss. Maintain source identities independently of coordinates.
requirements.acceptance: A function/composition example has a documented embedding/projection, explicit preserved information and visible ambiguity/loss when applicable.

requirements.title: Astra evidence upgrades
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Treat the inherited same-handler VERIFY as self-consistency. Assess transaction durability, authentication, branch/merge and identity limits before production reuse. Preserve packet-reported browser/Node/Python results and untested WebGL/device claims as historical evidence.
requirements.acceptance: Fresh adapter tests separate reused behavior, newly verified behavior and unsupported features; remote exposure uses the PolyIA access boundary, not Astra's unauthenticated loopback server unchanged.

requirements.title: TRE/TREE structural adapters
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Keep structural tree, coupling graph, render DAG and simulation model separate. Preserve content-addressed nodes and tree/graph compiler concepts without claiming a specified renderer is implemented. Replay must use actual full events, not merely rerunning the same fixture.
requirements.acceptance: Adapter fixtures identify each structure, test source-copy isolation and replay from retained events with all state-changing values.

requirements.title: SubstrateIO and ACSP continuity
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Preserve SubstrateIO's actual transition/history and authority contracts through versioned adapters. An observer reads history without advancing state. A source-named blocked research question stays blocked until its dependency is resolved.
requirements.acceptance: Read a real retained history through the adapter and verify that observations have no semantic effect or unauthorized continuity claim.

requirements.title: PURL and SEURL protocols
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Respect Programmable URL identities, GET-read/POST-effect boundaries, continuation verbs and authority constraints. Machine-readable URLs expose discoverable contracts and durable state; opening a URL must not silently execute an arbitrary mutation.
requirements.acceptance: Adapter tests distinguish inspection, admitted operation and continuation, with idempotent receipts and an unmodified upstream source snapshot.

requirements.title: CGT and GIN bridges
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Integrate actual published theory, executable examples, SDK/Grammar-as-a-Service material, operational semantics, costs and image/kernel distinctions from the pinned CGT and GIN repositories and books. Preserve existing theorem/definition identifiers.
requirements.acceptance: A source theorem/example is traceable into a PolyIA form, executed or cited under its real scope, and exported back with its original identity.

requirements.title: SNAD, Musa and specialist boundaries
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Map actual SNAD and Musa capabilities through their source-defined interfaces and domains. Preserve project policies, language records and provenance. Do not infer functionality merely from a repository name or previous narrative.
requirements.acceptance: Each adapter lists exact source files, inputs/outputs, tested behavior and unsupported areas; project-specific content restrictions remain enforceable.

requirements.title: Unavailable specialist adapters
requirements.title_group: Astra, geometry and canonical project adapters
requirements.mandate: Inventory PILLAR9, HOMELESS/Realms, Ingram, CIA Browser, QIA and other source-named systems. A seed/directive is not a completed runtime. Preserve their inherited constitutions as scoped obligations and provide real adapters only where executable sources and permissions exist.
requirements.acceptance: Capability registry marks available specification, available implementation, tested adapter and unresolved source separately; no pseudo-browser or invented engine fills a missing component.

requirements.title: Poly IA web application
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Deliver a usable application named Poly IA that presents the same underlying sources, state, scientific capabilities, guidance and evidence to humans and machine clients. The commission workbench starts first and grows into the research/concierge application.
requirements.acceptance: A browser and API client observe the same state revision and execute supported equivalent workflows with matching receipts.

requirements.title: Submission workspace
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Provide text/document/article intake with source preview, provenance, supported formats, scope and processing state. Preserve original material and let users inspect normalized forms and unresolved portions. A successful upload is not a successful interpretation.
requirements.acceptance: Intake tests show retained source bytes, staged processing, failure/ambiguity outcomes and resumable access to the submitted item's history.

requirements.title: Interpretation explorer
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Display recognized symbols, expressions, types, grammar memberships, operations, context, claims and source spans. Explain the interpretation path, alternatives and limits in understandable language. Unsupported portions remain first-class output.
requirements.acceptance: Selecting a construct resolves its source span, formal record, available operations, alternatives and evidence without requiring an LLM explanation.

requirements.title: Relations and opportunities explorer
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Show supported cross-domain relations and separate proposed opportunities. Distinguish semantic graph, hyperedge joint inputs and geometric layout. Users can inspect why a path is or is not admissible and what experiment would test a proposal.
requirements.acceptance: A mixed-source example shows a valid multi-input path and an invalid alternative with precise missing premises or context constraints.

requirements.title: Concierge compiler
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Accept supported native commissions and bounded natural-language intents, compile them into typed plans and offer ambiguous alternatives. Return executable artifacts, source/evidence links and expected costs before admitted effects. Unknown intent is a useful result.
requirements.acceptance: The polynomial teaching request and one non-mathematical request produce real plans and verified results without LLM inference, with unsupported requests explicitly bounded.

requirements.title: Source and book reader
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Make every retained book/source discoverable through its manifest and appropriate reader or download. Expose chapter/topic mappings and historical versions, preserving original labels without treating them as dispensable content.
requirements.acceptance: Corpus census and reader links include all canonical books and publication sources; selected source spans are readable and linked to derived claims.

requirements.title: Live progress and intervention
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Show commission requirements, produce/verify/accept receipts, queued research, failures, guidance inbox and applied changes. Real-time means a documented polling/event freshness contract; reconnects expose stale state until refreshed.
requirements.acceptance: Pause/resume, priority guidance and checkpoint inspection work through the UI; a disconnected browser does not display a false live indicator.

requirements.title: Stable API and client SDK
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Publish tested request/response schemas, pagination/event cursors, command IDs, revision behavior, error codes and capability discovery. Supply a small real client rather than a collection of illustrative request sketches.
requirements.acceptance: A clean client executes the documented flow, handles lost responses with idempotency and surfaces revision conflicts without silent rebasing.

requirements.title: Access and origin boundary
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Authenticate sensitive reads and authorize command scopes. Use TLS at the public boundary, strict origin/host rules, bounded JSON and safe rendering. Keep tokens out of URLs, source bundles and logs. Read tokens cannot mutate.
requirements.acceptance: Tests cover unauthenticated reads, read-only mutation, hostile origins/hosts, malformed/oversized JSON, XSS text and token redaction.

requirements.title: Accessibility and comprehensibility
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Make labels, focus order, status text, contrast and error feedback usable by keyboard and assistive technologies. Present mathematical assumptions and evidence grades beside results. Avoid making an ornamental visualization the only route to critical state.
requirements.acceptance: Human review covers keyboard navigation, small screens, readable equations, source access and understandable failure/connection feedback.

requirements.title: Human and machine parity
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Give each meaningful UI action a documented command or pure read. Let tools inspect and operate the system without scraping presentation text. Human-readable explanations remain derived from the same structured result and do not add unsupported claims.
requirements.acceptance: Parity tests compare UI-client and direct API actions, and the same result can be exported as structured JSON plus source-linked prose.

requirements.title: End-to-end native intake acceptance
requirements.title_group: Human/machine application and analytical workbench
requirements.mandate: Demonstrate the owner's principal use case: submit a prompt or article, identify supported structures, relate them through registered grammars, improve supported representations and emit experimentally testable opportunities. Preserve uncertainty and measure coverage; this is required without LLM inference.
requirements.acceptance: Held-out end-to-end fixtures include success, ambiguity, unsupported text, malicious instructions, contradictions and a bounded discovery proposal, with full source/evidence trace.

requirements.title: Oracle preflight and service installation
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Inspect the actual Oracle VM, mounted data, available runtime, storage, service manager, ports and current model/tool setup read-only. Use the established target and standing authority. Install the loopback state service under a supervisor, then configure the authenticated TLS boundary using actual provisioned values.
requirements.acceptance: Record real host/runtime inventory, service unit, persistence path, readiness, restart behavior and reachable URL; absent credentials/DNS remain explicit blockers rather than invented configuration.

requirements.title: Operational runbooks
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Provide installation, token provisioning/rotation, backup/restore, upgrades, migration, incident diagnosis, shutdown and recovery instructions. Distinguish bootstrap SQLite operations from later PostgreSQL/worker deployments. Preserve event/artifact durability during service upgrades.
requirements.acceptance: A fresh operator follows the runbook to start, inspect, back up, restore and verify the service using supplied commands and actual evidence.

requirements.title: Acceptance system
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Define mandatory test families and per-obligation evidence contracts, with PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, NOT_RUN and justified scoped exceptions. Evidence objects bind inputs, verifier, run, output bytes and applicable versions. A disabled test cannot count as a pass.
requirements.acceptance: Matrix linter covers all PIA and inherited obligations, verifies receipts and identifies every unresolved mandatory gate before shipment.

requirements.title: No-LLM and dependency gate
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Run the complete core acceptance workflows with optional model adapters disabled, no LLM weights and a declared minimal environment. Audit imports/processes/tools and run offline fixtures. Authorized source retrieval and web serving are separate capabilities from inference.
requirements.acceptance: Publish dependency/model audit, offline workflow logs and invocation records; local or remote inference cannot be concealed behind a renamed tool.

requirements.title: Release and destination repository
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Produce a reproducible source package, checksums, instructions, tests and a copyable start directive for the owner-supplied PolyIA repository. Preserve current remote work and use isolated branches where needed. Keep deployment/publishing claims tied to actions actually performed.
requirements.acceptance: Clean unpack verification passes; all relative links resolve; repository/deployment receipts state exact revisions and actual publication status.

requirements.title: Completion certificate
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Declare full commissioning complete only when the finite release contract, native intake workflow, live service, source custody, scientific acceptance, model/tool boundaries and research continuation all pass. An owner-approved amendment must identify excluded obligations and consequences explicitly.
requirements.acceptance: Final certificate enumerates accepted requirement versions, source manifest, test runs, live service checkpoint and remaining open scientific frontier; no blanket all-green prose substitutes for it.

requirements.title: University founding mandate
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: After commissioning, Poly IA develops Automaton Science University as a continuing institution for the science of forms, grammars, machines, generation, relations and evidence-governed evolution. Its mission connects basic constructs to higher-value reusable understanding without claims of material transmutation.
requirements.acceptance: Founding charter defines research objects, pedagogy, infrastructure, publications, review and the relationship to Substrate University, with source and epistemic continuity.

requirements.title: Open division research
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Develop VII and VIII through provisional charters, comparative research and evidence before making permanent disciplinary claims. Treat IX Infinity as the adopted division identity, with its calculus-of-forms program and links to DK0 and the rest of the University.
requirements.acceptance: Published charters include methods, falsifiable questions, milestones, negative results and boundaries; charter changes are versioned owner-visible decisions.

requirements.title: Curriculum, books and laboratories
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Generate source-linked courses, books, exercises and runnable laboratories from accepted knowledge and documented open problems. Include conventional mathematics and CS alongside house sciences without erasing the distinction. Keep all canonical books accessible.
requirements.acceptance: At least one course/lab path spans elementary operations, formal grammar, typed composition and verified experimentation with citations and reproducible exercises.

requirements.title: Research governance and replication
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Publish claims with data, code, assumptions, comparisons and counterexamples; invite independent replication through reproducible packages. Distinguish an innovation proposal, engineering improvement, empirical finding and proved theorem. Preserve null results and failed conjectures.
requirements.acceptance: A research publication template and completed example expose the evidence needed for another investigator to reproduce or refute the claim.

requirements.title: Standing continuous mandate
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Operate ongoing discovery under declared resource, authority and access policies. The owner can inspect, pause, guide and revise the mandate through the same acknowledged protocol. No promise of endless discovery overrides budgets, outages, missing evidence or human decisions.
requirements.acceptance: A supervised research cycle demonstrates pause/resume, budget exhaustion, restart continuity and a versioned admitted improvement or honestly reported null result.

requirements.title: Continuity beyond the commission
requirements.title_group: Deployment, acceptance and Automaton Science University
requirements.mandate: Keep every source, constitutional decision, experiment, package and university charter addressable across future revisions. New systems inherit explicit obligations and evidence rather than a compressed narrative memory. The final handoff identifies the next executable frontier and how any authorized collaborator resumes.
requirements.acceptance: A new reader/agent resumes from the final URL/checkpoint plus package alone, locates the controlling rules and continues without reconstructing hidden chat history.

requirements.title: Captured package artifact integrity
requirements.acceptance: Verify actual captured artifact bytes, without implying scientific correctness.

requirements.title: Registered exact scientific seed contracts
requirements.acceptance: Execute the registered acceptance family and require actual checks to pass.
